claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26 the Infrastructure Committee rejected administration's Recommendation 1 of report IS03688 (R), meaning either a motion to adopt R was put to a vote and defeated or a motion incompatible with R was carried. Also tested: whether R proposed a hold under claim 2's primary deferral definition, and whether the Infrastructure Committee or City Council had adopted R by 2026-09-25.
claims.interpretation_notes: (1) OPERATIVE VERSION. Under minutes item 1.4 the committee adopted its agenda with 'Replacement attachments: ... Attachments 2, 3, 5 (Version 1) and 5 (Version 2)', which added both replacements at the same time. Item 7.6 lists all three versions of Attachment 5. Neither the agenda nor the minutes says which version was before the committee when it considered the item, so the operative version is uncertain. Per the brief I use Version 2 (DocumentId 304030) as the primary reading. For the 14 routes it lists apart, R's treatment in the attachment's own words is: 'The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications. In Q1 2027, Administration will bring forward a report outlining trade-offs and options for the remaining routes, including an update on the remaining funding and budget implications, for Council direction and approval.' It also says: 'If Council approves the approach, the following projects may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches.' Version 2 never says in terms that construction or advancement of those routes waits for the evaluation or the report. That is implied by the contrast with 'will continue as planned', but it is not stated. So under the primary reading Version 2 is not a hold (see claim 2). The original (304032) is a hold: the listed projects 'would be removed from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027' until after an evaluation. Version 1 (304031) is a hold under its rules 1a and 1b, which remove routes that affect travel lanes or parking. Councillor Salvador's notice of motion (committee item 11.1) quotes a section heading, 'Will be reevaluated for feasibility and subject to funding availability', that appears only in the original and Version 1. This hints at which text members were reading but does not establish which version was operative. (2) DISPOSITION OF ITEM 7.6. The carried minutes of item 7.6 record no motion to adopt R, whether moved, put or defeated. The only substantive motion was Councillor A. Salvador's: continue the programme 'in accordance with the previously approved scope of Capital Profile CM-20-0330', immediately advance procurement for tender-ready routes, and schedule 2027 construction at the earliest feasible opportunity. That motion is incompatible with R. It was put and Defeated 2 to 2: A. Salvador and M. Janz in favour, E. Rutherford and R. Clarke opposed. Councillor E. Rutherford's amendment deleting 'and maximize remaining construction season, including advancing partial and accelerated construction' was also Defeated 2 to 2: Rutherford and Clarke in favour, Salvador and Janz opposed. The only other carried motion on the item was E. Rutherford's 'That Attachment 4 ... remain private' (Carried 4 to 0: Rutherford, Salvador, Clarke, Janz). That motion mirrors R's companion Recommendation 2, and was carried as a committee decision, not as a recommendation to Council. The procedural motions to meet in private and in public both carried 5 to 0. So the committee 'left R without a decision' as the brief defines it: every substantive motion failed and nothing adopting R was moved. (3) CLASSIFICATION. Under Version 2, R did not propose a hold, so the verdict is Partially supported. What is established: R was not adopted by any body. What is not established: that what the committee declined was a hold, or that members voted R down or voted to go ahead against it; no motion incompatible with R carried. Under the original and Version 1, R proposed a hold, and the verdict is still Partially supported, on the 'left without a decision' row. The claim-1 verdict therefore does not depend on which version was operative. (4) REQUIRED ALTERNATIVE READING ('did not support' = non-adoption): Supported. Neither the committee nor City Council adopted R by 2026-09-25. (5) REQUIRED ALTERNATIVE BODY (City Council): Not established. Neither R nor the report appears in the carried City Council minutes from 2026-08-26 to 2026-09-25. The only related Council item is item 11.6 at the meeting of 2026-09-08 (meeting id 3195d7e4-...): Councillor Salvador's notice of motion, first given at Executive Committee on 2026-09-02, asking for options to increase CM-20-0330 funding in the 2027-2030 budget. It was 'Laid Over: September 8, 2026, City Council to October 6, 2026, City Council'. That motion is not R and does not decide it. A body that never received R cannot have supported or rejected it. (6) QUALIFICATION 2, MEMBERSHIP. The committee members present were Councillors E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz and A. Paquette, plus Mayor A. Knack as a member under section 15(3) of Bylaw 18156. Paquette was absent with notice for part of the meeting. On the amendment and on the main motion, neither Knack nor Paquette is recorded as voting. The minutes note Paquette's partial absence; they do not give a reason for Knack's absence from those votes. Councillors M. Elliott, J. Morgan, T. Parmar, K. Principe, A. Stevenson, K. Tang and J. Wright attended but were not committee members and had no vote. (7) QUALIFICATION 4, OVERRIDE STRAND. On item 7.6 the committee decided only that Attachment 4 remain private. It made no decision on R, adopting or rejecting, that a later body could override. No later City Council decision incompatible with any committee decision on item 7.6 appears by 2026-09-25. The minutes therefore show no override. The commenters' 'ignore a committee's decision' has no committee decision on R to refer to. (8) QUALIFICATION 5, WHAT GOVERNED AFTER 2026-08-26. The previously approved scope of CM-20-0330 continued to govern: $100,000,000 under Capital Budget Amendment 7 as re-stated, Carried 9 to 4, City Council Budget meeting of 2022-11-30 and continuations. So did Council's 2026-07-07 item 7.5 decision to amend the scope of the 50 Street project (Carried 9 to 3). What follows are administration's statements, not Council decisions. IS03688 says that 'for routes where construction has not yet started, construction is best postponed to 2027'. Attachment 3's footnote 2 says three tendered routes 'may be delayed (in whole or in part) to 2027 or removed ... pending this Council report'. Its footnote 1 says the southern segment of 50 Street 'has been paused for reconsideration'. Taproot Edmonton (2026-09-01) reports that the City's project page described Grovenor as cancelled and 101 Avenue and 95 Avenue as deferred under administration's delegated authority (https://edmonton.taproot.news/news/2026/09/01/bike-routes-cancelled-or-put-off-despite-council-direction). I could not retrieve the City page (HTTP 502 twice), so that account is a media lead only. It is not a decision of the committee or of Council.

claims.proposition_evaluated: In report IS03688 for the Infrastructure Committee of 2026-08-26, administration recommended an approach that expressly defers construction or advancement of 14 named routes of the programme, all unbuilt at 2026-08-10, until a further evaluation, report or decision. Operative version: Version 2 (DocumentId 304030), declared primary because the record does not show which version was before the committee.
claims.interpretation_notes: RECOMMENDATION 1 asks for approval of the approach in Attachment 5 ('That Infrastructure Committee recommend to City Council: 1. That the updated approach for the remaining routes ... as outlined in Attachment 5 ... be approved'). The requested action is 'Council decision required'. OPERATIVE VERSION: uncertain. Minutes item 1.4 added replacements 5 (Version 1) and 5 (Version 2) together, and item 7.6 lists all three versions. Version 2 is used as primary. PASSAGES QUOTED. Original (304032): 'If Council approves the recommended change in approach, the following projects would be removed from the scope of the Active Transportation Network Expansion Program for 2026 and 2027. After Administration evaluates any applicable changes in municipal bike lane authority and subject to available funding following the completion of other scheduled routes, these routes may be revisited using alternate design approaches under the current Program or other future initiatives.' Its rules 1a and 1b also say routes that impact travel lanes or parking 'will be removed from the Active Transportation Network Expansion Program'. Version 1 (304031): the same rules 1a and 1b, the same section heading 'Will be reevaluated for feasibility and subject to funding availability', and the list passage 'If Council approves the recommended change in approach, the following projects may be revisited using alternate design approaches or other future initiatives.' Version 2 (304030): 'The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications. In Q1 2027, Administration will bring forward a report outlining trade-offs and options for the remaining routes, including an update on the remaining funding and budget implications, for Council direction and approval.' and 'If Council approves the approach, the following projects may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches.' CLASSIFICATION BY VERSION. Original: primary deferral met, because the routes are removed from scope for 2026-2027 until evaluation and funding allow; the stricter alternative is also met ('removed from the scope'). Version 1: primary met, because rules 1a/1b remove the affected routes and rule 3a reassesses them only after the remaining routes are complete. The stricter alternative is met only if rules 1a/1b are read onto the listed routes; the list passage itself does not say they are removed. Version 2: primary not met. The text sets out evaluation and a report back but never says the listed routes wait for that step; the wait is implied only by the contrast with 'will continue as planned'. The stricter alternative is not met. COUNT, identical in all three versions. Listed apart (14): 50 Street (101 Avenue to 109A Avenue); 64 Street (119 Avenue to Yellowhead Trail); 79 Street (76 Avenue to 101 Avenue); 84 Avenue (79 Street to 83 Street); 85 Street (93 Avenue to 98 Avenue); 88 Avenue/93 Street/87 Avenue (85 Street to 96 Street); 89 Street (76 Avenue to Connors Road); 92A Avenue/86 Street/alley (Connors Road to 85 Street); 93 Street (82 Avenue to 84 Avenue) and 84 Avenue (91 Street to 89 Street); 93 Avenue/82 Street/94 Avenue (85 Street to 75 Street) and 75 Street (94 Avenue to 94B Avenue); 95 Avenue (142 Street to 163 Street); 101 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); 106 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); Grovenor - 148 Street, 104 Avenue and 144 Street. Continue as planned (13): 50 Street (109A Avenue to Goldbar Park Road); 84 Avenue (Mill Creek Ravine to 91 Street); 100 Street (76 Avenue to 80 Avenue); 107 Avenue (East of Groat Road to 163 Street); 110 Avenue/90 Street and 112 Avenue; 111 Avenue (120 Street to 121 Street); 114 Avenue (81 Street to 89 Street); 127 Avenue (97 Street to 102A Street); 163 Street from 87 Avenue to 95 Avenue; 163 Street (Stony Plain Road to 107 Avenue); 167 Street/169 Street (Whitemud Drive to 87 Avenue); Kingsway (113 Street to 122 Street); Victoria Park Road (116 Street to River Valley Road). Splitting the multi-segment bullets (the 93 Street/84 Avenue bullet +1, the 93 Avenue.../75 Street bullet +1, Grovenor +2) would give 18; this is the reviewer's count. STATUS at 2026-08-10, from Attachment 3 (original 304029 and replacement 304028, which give the same per-route statuses). 84 Avenue (79–83 Street), 92A Avenue/86 Street/alley, and 93 Street/84 Avenue: 'Tender awarded. Construction has not yet started.' Attachment 3 names the last as '93 Street/84 Avenue (89 Street to 82 Avenue)', matched to Attachment 5's entry. 64 Street, 79 Street, 85 Street, 88 Avenue/93 Street/87 Avenue, 89 Street, and 93 Avenue/82 Street/94 Avenue and 75 Street: 'originally scheduled for construction in 2026 ... installation in 2026 is no longer viable'. 50 Street (101–109A Avenue), 95 Avenue, 101 Avenue, 106 Avenue and Grovenor: under 'Other', 'do not have a delivery plan and schedule at this time'. Footnote 1 says the 50 Street southern section 'has been paused for reconsideration'. None of the 14 appears among the routes recorded as under construction, so all 14 are unbuilt at the primary date. ALTERNATIVE STATUS DATE (2026-08-26): I found no City record dated 2026-08-26 that gives per-route status. Both Attachment 3 versions are dated 'as of August 10, 2026', and the item 7.6 presentation was not available. Under the alternative all 14 are therefore unresolved; no route is shown to differ. VERDICT: under Version 2 (primary), the count is 14 and all are unbuilt, but the primary deferral reading is not met, so the verdict is Partially supported. Under the original and Version 1 it would be Supported. The finding is version-sensitive. Qualification 3, budget, in the report's words: the recommendations 'would not result in any changes required to the existing capital profile CM-20-0330 ... or associated borrowing bylaws'.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Between 2022-11-30 and 2026-09-25, Councillors K. Principe and J. Rice brought (moved or seconded) two motions at City Council. Each would have left the approved capital budget of CM-20-0330 at $45,000,000 to $55,000,000, and each directed the released funds to a named destination. Council defeated both.
claims.interpretation_notes: MOTIONS FOUND. (A) Fall 2023 Supplemental Capital Budget Adjustment, City Council Budget meeting of 2023-11-21 and continuations, Capital Budget Amendment 2. Moved by K. Principe, seconded by J. Rice. As first moved: 'That composite profile CM-20-0330 - Active Transportation be decreased by $50,000,000 to go towards the tax levy.' As re-stated and put: 'That capital profile CM-20-0330 - Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 be reduced by $50,000,000 ($16,350,000 in 2024, $16,825,000 in 2025, and $16,825,000 in 2026) with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt.' Defeated 4 to 8. In favour: S. Hamilton, T. Cartmell, J. Rice, K. Principe. Opposed: A. Knack, A. Paquette, A. Sohi, A. Salvador, K. Tang, E. Rutherford, A. Stevenson, J. Wright. M. Janz is not recorded. (B) Fall 2024 Supplemental Capital Budget Adjustment, City Council Budget meeting of 2024-12-02 and continuations, Capital Budget Amendment 2. Moved by K. Principe, seconded by J. Rice: 'That capital profile CM-20-0330 - Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 be decreased by $33,650,000 in 2025 and $33,650,000 in 2026 with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund planning, design and delivery of the Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 project.' Defeated 4 to 7. In favour: T. Cartmell, J. Rice, E. Rutherford, K. Principe. Opposed: A. Knack, A. Sohi, A. Salvador, M. Janz, K. Tang, A. Stevenson, J. Wright. S. Hamilton is not recorded, and A. Paquette was absent with notice. BASE: $100,000,000 ($5,950,000 in 2023, $26,750,000 in 2024, $33,650,000 in 2025, $33,650,000 in 2026), from Capital Budget Amendment 7 as re-stated and carried 9 to 4 at the 2022-11-30 budget meeting. IS03688 (2026) also says '$100 million was approved'. I could not read the capital profile attachments (FCS01698 Att. 2; FCS02053; FCS02530rev; FCS03130 Att. 3), so any adjustment to the total before each motion is unverified. ARITHMETIC (reviewer's calculation). A: $16,350,000 + $16,825,000 + $16,825,000 = $50,000,000 cut; $100,000,000 − $50,000,000 = $50,000,000 remaining. That is inside the $45M–$55M band and a cut of exactly half. B: $33,650,000 × 2 = $67,300,000 cut; $100,000,000 − $67,300,000 = $32,700,000 remaining. That is outside the band, and the cut is more than half. B could meet the band only if the base were between $112,300,000 and $122,300,000. Nothing indicates that. B's two annual figures equal the 2025 and 2026 amounts approved in 2022. DESTINATIONS. A, as put: 'with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt', which I read as a reduction in borrowing and so a named destination. A's original wording named 'the tax levy'. B: 'with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund planning, design and delivery'. I read that as a reduction in borrowing, but it can also be read as merely naming the funding source, in which case B names no destination. Neither text names another programme or priority. BROUGHT: both motions were moved by Principe and seconded by Rice, on separate occasions. They therefore meet both the primary reading and the co-sponsorship alternative. DEFEATED: both were put to recorded votes at City Council and lost. CLASSIFICATION. Primary: A meets every element; B fails the $45M–$55M band. Supported is therefore unavailable, and at least one jointly brought reduction motion was defeated, so the verdict is Partially supported. Alternative amount band (cut of at least half): A and B both meet it. If B's debt phrase counts as a destination, the result would be Supported; if not, Partially supported. The finding is definition-sensitive. The co-sponsorship alternative gives the same result as the primary. QUALIFICATION 4, OTHER MOTIONS. (i) 2023-11 Capital Budget Amendment 3, moved by J. Rice and seconded by K. Principe: '$26,808,000 be reduced from the 2024 capital budget ...'. Its text does not name CM-20-0330, and it was withdrawn, not defeated. (ii) City Council 2025-09-16, item 10.13, moved by T. Cartmell and seconded by K. Principe: that construction 'cease immediately on bike lane projects ... where construction has not yet started, pending a complete review'. Defeated 4 to 9, with Rice in favour. This is a pause motion, not a budget cut. (iii) At the 2022-11-30 budget meeting, Rice and Principe voted against Capital Budget Amendment 7 ($100,000,000). claims.suggested_one_line: Principe and Rice did bring two motions to cut the bike-lane programme, and Council defeated both. The 2023 motion would have cut it to $50 million; the 2024 motion would have cut it further, to about $32.7 million.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Mostly. In November 2023, Councillor Principe moved and Councillor Rice seconded a motion cutting the $100 million programme by $50 million through reduced borrowing; Council defeated it 4–8. In December 2024 the same pair moved to remove the programme's 2025 and 2026 funding, $67.3 million in total, which would have left about $32.7 million (reviewer's calculation); Council defeated it 4–7. So both attempts happened and both lost, but only the first matches 'cut it to $50M'. Neither motion's text names another priority for the money, only lower borrowing.
suggested_tldr: Two motions, both Principe/Rice, both defeated: 4–8 in 2023 and 4–7 in 2024.
Only the 2023 motion would have left $50M; the 2024 motion would have left about $32.7M.
The only destination either motion names is reduced tax-supported debt.
